item.title: Sicario 3: Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro, Josh Brolin reunite for third film
item.description: Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro and Josh Brolin are officially returning for 'Sicario 3', reuniting the core trio from the acclaimed 2015 crime thriller for the franchise’s third instalment.
item.content:encoded:
Sicario 3: Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro, Josh Brolin reunite for third film Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro and Josh Brolin are officially returning for 'Sicario 3', reuniting the core trio from the acclaimed 2015 crime thriller for the franchise’s third instalment. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 14:13 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 14:13 IST

Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro, Josh Brolin (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro and Josh Brolin are officially returning for 'Sicario 3', reuniting the core trio from the acclaimed 2015 crime thriller for the franchise’s third instalment. The three actors are set to reprise their iconic roles, bringing back the central cast of 'Sicario' for the upcoming film. Plot details are being kept tightly under wraps, as per Deadline. Padraic McKinley, who directed 'The Weight', has been chosen to helm the third film following a search involving the producers and lead cast. Oscar nominee Steven Knight has penned the latest draft of the screenplay, as per Deadline. McKinley and Knight are currently polishing the script based on feedback from the cast. The film is being produced by Black Label Media, with Molly Smith, Trent Luckinbill and Thad Luckinbill attached, and Thunder Road, with Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee and returning producer Ed McDonnell. Producers are planning to begin production at the top of the year. The first two films in the franchise were distributed by Lionsgate, including the original 'Sicario' in 2015 and 2018’s 'Sicario: Day of the Soldado'. However, 'Sicario 3' is currently being taken to the open market, with multiple studios showing strong interest in the project. With Blunt, Del Toro and Brolin all returning, the third film brings the franchise’s core trio back together as development moves towards production. (ANI)

item.title: Trump warns Iran, open to direct talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump warned Iran of severe consequences if it issued threats prompting the relocation of US aircraft from Britain. Despite blaming Iran for regional tensions and a Flydubai ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump warns Iran, open to direct talks US President Donald Trump warned Iran of severe consequences if it issued threats prompting the relocation of US aircraft from Britain. Despite blaming Iran for regional tensions and a Flydubai incident, Trump stated he remains open to direct talks and expressed optimism about falling energy prices. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 12:59 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 12:59 IST

United States President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

United States President Donald Trump issued a stern warning that Tehran would “suffer greatly” if found responsible for security threats that prompted Washington to relocate military aircraft from Britain, whilst simultaneously affirming that he remained receptive to direct talks with Iranian leadership. Addressing journalists prior to his departure aboard Marine One, President Trump responded to queries concerning Middle Eastern tensions, energy markets, US bomber repositioning, and an incident involving Flydubai. When questioned regarding whether a specific threat triggered the decision to withdraw bombers from British soil, President Trump verified that threats had indeed been received. He remarked, “Yeah, I think we can say that. I mean, they didn't fly out by accident, yeah.” Elaborating further, President Trump stated, “No, but there were some threats and, rather than tempting the enemy, we'll capture the enemy and beat the enemy. But why should we leave them there? So, we moved them around a little bit, not very far.” Although initial inquiries did not immediately pinpoint the source of the danger, subsequent questioning probed whether combat drones might have been introduced into Britain, prompting the tactical repositioning. In response, President Trump stated, “I can't tell you that but if they did, they'll suffer greatly.” The US leader subsequently revealed that American intelligence had identified those accountable for the security warnings. Stating that authorities possessed specific knowledge regarding the perpetrators, President Trump noted, “So, we had a threat and if we're going to be threatened, we'll just move them and that sort of alleviates that. And we actually know the people that made the threat and they've got themselves a big problem.” When explicitly pressed on whether those individuals bore connections to Iran, he affirmed, “They would be linked to Iran.” Despite the security concerns, President Trump maintained confidence in the host nation, noting continued operational security and cooperation. When asked if Britain remained a secure environment for American personnel, he replied, “I think it is and I have a very good relationship with your new prime minister.” Notwithstanding his direct cautions to Tehran, the US President indicated a willingness to engage diplomatically, offering a brief affirmation when asked if he was open to direct talks. During the exchange, President Trump also alleged that Tehran bore culpability for an airborne security incident involving Flydubai, stating, “I do; I personally do,” though he offered no further elaboration or documentary proof during his remarks. Shifting towards economic indicators, fuel costs, and disruptions affecting Russian refining infrastructure, President Trump expressed optimism regarding commodity trends. He observed, “Gasoline prices are going down very rapidly. When the war ends, they'll drop like a rock and the war is going to end very soon.” While acknowledging that strikes on Russian refineries had generated constraints concerning diesel availability, prompting both Washington and European partners to tap strategic reserves, President Trump reiterated his administration's broader geopolitical stance, “And oil prices are coming down and here’s the nice part, Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” (ANI)

item.title: US monitors suspected plague case in Russian lab worker amid fears of internal spread, says Rubio
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington is closely monitoring a suspected plague case at a Russian laboratory amid concerns of internal spread. While travel between the US and Russia ...
item.content:encoded:
US monitors suspected plague case in Russian lab worker amid fears of internal spread, says Rubio US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington is closely monitoring a suspected plague case at a Russian laboratory amid concerns of internal spread. While travel between the US and Russia is limited, officials are watching the situation closely as a precaution. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 09:52 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 09:52 IST

United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington is closely observing a suspected plague case involving a laboratory employee in Russia, amid apprehensions that the contagion could have undergone internal transmission. He noted that Washington's intelligence regarding the event remains restricted to details supplied by Russian officials, though US authorities are keeping a close watch due to the inherent risk of infectious diseases migrating beyond their initial source. Whilst addressing reporters at Joint Base Andrews prior to setting off on a European visit, Rubio remarked, “We don't - we know what we know, obviously, about whatever the Russians have provided, which is it seems that there was a worker at the lab that was infected, and there's concern that that could have spread, at least internally." He further observed, “So you've seen them do quarantines with this - of that nature." Rubio emphasised that travel between the United States and Russia remains constrained, yet affirmed that Washington treats the scenario with gravity owing to potential wider dissemination risks. He stated, “There's very limited travel between the US and Russia, obviously. But like anything else, something like that gets out, it could quickly spread." He added, “So we're watching and monitoring it closely. I don't think it's cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause to just keep an eye on it, and we're doing that." Rubio refrained from specifying the particular Russian facility, the geographical site of the suspected contamination, or the specific variant of plague involved. Furthermore, he did not clarify whether American personnel independently verified the infection. His observations suggested that the intelligence accessible to Washington originated directly from Moscow. The remarks occurred during an extensive dialogue with journalists encompassing various topics, including Russia's ongoing conflict in Ukraine, Yemen, Saudi Arabia, American military troop postings stationed in Britain, alongside the administration's strategic long-term national security framework. When questioned separately regarding Moscow prompting foreign diplomatic personnel stationed in Kyiv to evacuate the Ukrainian capital, Rubio noted that Russian authorities have disseminated similar advisories across multiple months. He stated that the United States maintains its diplomatic footprint inside Kyiv and will independently evaluate local security conditions. Rubio declared, “We analyse every single day the safety of every diplomatic mission in the world, and if a threat arises that we feel needs to be addressed by a change in posture, we'll do so." He continued, “We haven't done that up to this point there." Rubio faced additional inquiries concerning the relocation of American bomber aircraft departing from RAF Fairford in Britain following a security alert the preceding week. He advised against drawing direct links between aircraft redeployments and the security warning, explaining that US military equipment and personnel undergo frequent rotation and repositioning. He stated, “The Department of War is constantly reallocating resources where they need to be." When asked if Washington retains trust in British security measures governing the installation, Rubio responded affirmatively. He stated, “We have confidence in the security of all of our bases, because all of our bases are theoretically - could be threatened at any moment, and that's why there's so much security built around them." Rubio mentioned that British officials collaborated closely alongside the United States throughout the inquiry into the security threat. Plague is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and occurs in several forms, including bubonic, septicaemic and pneumonic plague. The risk of transmission varies by form, with pneumonic plague capable of spreading between people through respiratory droplets. (ANI)

item.description: US President Donald Trump has approved a firing-squad execution for former Army psychiatrist Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting that killed 13 people. This marks the US ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump approves firing-squad execution of 2009 Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan US President Donald Trump has approved a firing-squad execution for former Army psychiatrist Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting that killed 13 people. This marks the US military's first approved execution since 1961. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 09:50 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 09:50 IST

Handout photo of Nidal Hasan, who was convicted in connection with the 2009 Fort Hood shooting that killed 13 people and injured 31 others (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States military has advanced significantly towards carrying out the execution of Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan, who was convicted of murdering 13 individuals and wounding over 30 others during the 2009 mass shooting incident at Fort Hood, Texas. The Pentagon announced on Monday that President Donald Trump has authorised his execution via firing squad, a method unutilised by the US military since 1961. Should this proceeding occur, Hasan's execution will represent the first military execution carried out by the United States armed forces in decades. The 2009 atrocity additionally resulted in over two dozen individuals sustaining injuries. In a statement posted on X, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell declared, “US War Secretary Pete Hegseth has recommended, and President Donald J. Trump has approved, death by US Army firing squad for convicted terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan." Parnell further wrote, “The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come." A military jury delivered a death sentence against Hasan in 2013 following his conviction relating to the Fort Hood mass shooting, an assault prosecutors argued stemmed from Al-Qaeda inspiration. Throughout his court-martial proceedings, Hasan chose self-representation, refrained from summoning witnesses, declined to offer testimony, and made no effort to dispute the formal charges. His court-appointed defence counsel had previously voiced apprehensions that he was actively pursuing a death sentence. Hasan, a US-born Muslim of Palestinian heritage, commenced firing on November 5, 2009, inside a medical building situated within the extensive Fort Hood military base. The installation served as a principal staging area supporting US military personnel preparing for combat deployments throughout Iraq and Afghanistan. Amongst the fatalities, twelve victims were soldiers, whilst the thirteenth was a civilian. Furthermore, thirty individuals suffered wounds during the incident. Responding civilian police officers shot and partially paralysed Hasan during the engagement. Testimony presented during the trial revealed that Hasan opposed US military campaigns in Iraq and Afghanistan. Evidence also showed he maintained online communications with Anwar al-Awlaki, an American-born radical cleric connected to Al-Qaeda who subsequently perished in a US drone strike conducted in Yemen. Whilst mass shootings remain relatively frequent across the United States, incidents occurring within US military installations happen less regularly. During 2025, a soldier initiated gunfire at a US military base located in Georgia, injuring five fellow service members before being subdued and arrested. In 2019, a US Navy sailor fatally shot two individuals and wounded another at a military facility in Hawaii. Throughout that same year, a Saudi military student killed three people at a US facility situated in Florida. During 2015, a US citizen of Kuwaiti birth targeted two military facilities in Tennessee, ending the lives of four Marines and a sailor. Subsequent investigations by the FBI determined that the assault derived inspiration from a “foreign terrorist group". Two years prior, a gunman killed 12 individuals and wounded eight others at the Washington Navy Yard in the US capital, before police officers shot and killed the assailant. (ANI)
